title: Terms for Claimant Identity Verification Appointments
content:
Video and appointment-based in-person pathways of Claimant Identity Verification are booked as appointments; a walk-in pathway may also be completed without one. The following terms apply to every appointment.

## Terms

(a) **When an appointment can be booked.** An appointment may be booked only while the case status is opened or in progress, as shown on the case record at the time of booking.

(b) **Earliest date and latest date.** The earliest bookable date is the pathway's minimum lead business days after the scheduling date, counted in business days (Monday through Friday excluding state holidays), and an appointment is never booked after the verification deadline.

(c) **Changing a booking.** A booking may be changed no more than the pathway's reschedule limit. Reschedules are counted over the life of the case as the appointments booked on the case less one, because the first booking is not a reschedule, and the count is never below zero.

(d) **Cancelling and missing.** An appointment cancelled at least the cancellation notice hours before its start is not missed; otherwise a no-show is recorded as a missed appointment, and when the number of missed appointments on the case reaches the pathway's missed-appointment limit the case is failed.

(e) **Interpreter and session length.** A free interpreter is provided where the pathway offers one, and the session is booked for the pathway's visit length.


## Applying the terms (hypothetical figures; no state holiday falls in any span shown)

**Lead time.** With a lead of 2 business days and a booking made on a Thursday, the first business day after it is Friday and the second is Monday, so Monday is the earliest bookable date. With a lead of 1 business day and a booking made on a Friday, Monday is the earliest bookable date.

**Deadline.** For a case whose verification deadline is 22 March, an appointment on 22 March may be booked; an appointment on 23 March may not.

**Cancellation notice.** With a 24-hour notice requirement and an appointment at 10:00 on a Wednesday, a cancellation at 09:00 on the Tuesday (25 hours before) is not a missed appointment. A cancellation at 15:00 on the Tuesday (19 hours before) does not meet the notice, and if the claimant then does not attend, a missed appointment is recorded.

**Reschedules.** A case with three appointments booked over its life has 2 reschedules; a case with one booking has none.

**Missed limit.** On a pathway with a missed-appointment limit of 2, the second missed appointment on the case fails the case.

| Case status at booking | Appointment may be booked |
|---|---|
| opened | yes |
| in progress | yes |
| verified, failed, expired, fraud confirmed or closed | no |
